newsitem.title: FRANCE: French haulage bosses say pay offer "flexible".
newsitem.headline: French haulage bosses say pay offer "flexible".

text.p: France's road haulage employers said on Thursday their pay offer, rejected as insufficient by striking truck drivers, was open to amendment and urged truckers to end their blockade of French roads.

Asked whether the employers were prepared to make a fresh offer to help end the 11-day-old blockade that is strangling the economy, Jean-Louis Amato, president of the Unostra hauliers' association, said the offer of a one percent real pay rise and a 1,500 franc ($300) one-time bonus was "flexible".
Speaking on behalf of the four employers' federations, Rene Petit told a news conference: "We have the feeling that major progress has been made. We have made a big effort."
He said no renegotiation was planned beyond working groups on the definition of truck drivers' duties and working hours agreed upon in talks that ended around midnight.

The government ended its mediation in the dispute, saying the drivers' main demands -- retirement at 55 instead of 60 and payment for loading and compulsory rest periods -- had been met and urging them to return to work. But strikers voted to maintain their blockade to demand a better deal on pay.
"The mediation ended last night, but we have in no way said we are breaking off (dialogue with the unions)," said Claude Leroy of the FFOCT employers' federation.
